platform_genre: 3D third-person action roguelite (run-based, single-player OR up to 4-player co-op) by Hopoo Games, published by Gearbox; ongoing development since 2022 handed to Gearbox/an internal team. Real-time manual combat: WASD move + jump + primary/secondary/utility/special abilities, all skill-shot/aimed, with active dodging and positioning (no auto-aim). A run = descend through procedurally-composed stages, clear a Teleporter event boss, advance; power comes ENTIRELY from stacking dropped items mid-run (no between-run stat currency). Platforms: PC/Steam, PS4/PS5, Xbox, Switch, mobile ports exist but the design canon is PC/console. This is the closest AAA-scale sibling to Abyssal Lantern's 'manual, telegraphed, skill-based action' pillar, unlike the auto-fire Vampire Survivors cluster. Sources: https://store.steampowered.com/app/632360/Risk_of_Rain_2/ , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_of_Rain_2
difficulty_ceiling_endless: TWO layered endless models plus a gated modifier ladder -- the richest GAP-A case in this cohort. (1) CONTINUOUS TIME-SCALING: a hidden 'difficulty coefficient' rises every second (linearly with time) and jumps hard on each stage transition (compounds with stages completed), so enemies perpetually outscale you unless you keep collecting items -- the community rule of thumb is ~1 item/minute. The named difficulty bands (Drizzle/Rainstorm/Monsoon and beyond up to HAHAHAHA) just change the coefficient's slope/starting value. (2) LOOPING: the run is endless by default -- after stage 5 (Sky Meadow) you can align the Primordial Teleporter to loop back to stage 1 instead of ending, repeating forever with the coefficient still climbing; you choose when to stop (fight Mithrix, obliterate at the Celestial Portal, or die). (3) ECLIPSE (E1-E8): a separate CLEAR-TO-UNLOCK modifier ladder -- each level stacks a permanent handicap (E1 -50% start HP, E2 smaller teleporter zone, E3 lethal fall damage, E4 faster enemies, E5 -50% healing, E6 less gold, E7 shorter enemy cooldowns, E8 permanent max-HP-loss-on-hit) and you must WIN a run (beat Mithrix) to unlock the next level, tracked INDEPENDENTLY PER SURVIVOR. Sources: https://riskofrain2.fandom.com/wiki/Difficulty , https://riskofrain2.fandom.com/wiki/Looping , https://riskofrain2.fandom.com/wiki/Eclipse , https://www.reddit.com/r/riskofrain/
fail_forward_meta: MINIMAL / almost none by design -- a deliberate contrast to Abyssal Lantern's 40%-XP + 100%-Shard carryover. A lost run grants NO persistent power: you always restart at level 1 with base stats and zero items. The ONLY thing a run leaves behind is horizontal UNLOCKS (survivors/items/equipment/artifacts) IF you happened to complete the tied challenge that run, and Steam/logbook records. There is no defeat-currency, no partial-XP salvage, no meta stat tree. Eclipse even punishes failure by holding you at your current level until you achieve a WIN, so failed Eclipse attempts advance nothing. The 'progression' RoR2 offers on loss is purely player knowledge + pool variety. Sources: https://riskofrain2.fandom.com/wiki/Challenges , https://www.reddit.com/r/riskofrain/ (meta-progression threads)
build_depth_and_solved_build_defense: Extremely deep IN-RUN, and a canonical GAP-C cautionary tale. Depth comes from stacking dozens of items whose scaling type varies: LINEAR (Lens-Maker's Glasses/Crowbar add flat % per stack, some hard-cap e.g. 10 glasses = 100% crit), HYPERBOLIC (Tougher Times block-chance, Safer Spaces -- diminishing, asymptotes below 100% so no true invuln), and MULTIPLICATIVE/EFFECTIVELY-EXPONENTIAL (Gasoline, Shuriken scale two attributes at once so power grows quadratically+). The real runaway engine is PROC CHAINS via hidden 'proc coefficients': one hit can trigger Ukulele->AtG Missile->Charged Perforator->Shatterspleen cascades, amplified by 57 Leaf Clover (luck) -- a single attack deletes the screen. Result: late runs become BINARY -- 'delete or be deleted' -- you either out-scale and one-shot everything or get one-shot yourself, which is exactly the 'solved-build trivializes the run' failure mode. SOLVED-BUILD PRESSURE: certain items are auto-picks (Shaped Glass, proc enablers, Gesture of the Drowned + equipment, Bungus/N'kuhana healing-to-damage), and the unlockable COMMAND artifact lets you hand-pick every item drop, letting players deterministically assemble the known-broken build and remove all run-to-run variety. RoR2's only real 'defense' is the ever-rising time coefficient (a solved build still needs to be assembled fast enough) and Eclipse handicaps -- NOT any nerf/soft-cap on the dominant combos themselves. Sources: https://riskofrain2.fandom.com/wiki/Proc_Coefficient , https://riskofrain2.fandom.com/wiki/Item , https://riskofrain2.fandom.com/wiki/Artifact_of_Command , https://www.reddit.com/r/riskofrain/ (busted-build/one-shot-meta threads)
retention_return_hook: Several stacked, mostly NON-daily hooks, plus one true recurring hook. (a) ECLIPSE grind -- climb E1->E8 for EACH survivor independently, a huge per-character mastery treadmill that is the primary long-tail retention. (b) UNLOCK CHASE -- survivors/items/equipment/artifacts/Mastery skins gated behind specific challenges pull you back to attempt new feats. (c) PRISMATIC TRIALS -- the closest thing to a daily/recurring loop: a solo mode on a FIXED shared seed (same map/items/enemies for everyone) that ROTATES on a timer (community reports ~every 72h), with a global + friends leaderboard; it's built for competitive route/skill optimization on identical conditions. (d) LOOPING/high-score self-competition. IMPORTANT CAVEAT for us: the Prismatic leaderboard is widely regarded as broken -- top times are cheated/exploited, it frequently fails to load, and mods disable submission -- so the recurring-hook execution is a WARNING as much as a template. Sources: https://riskofrain2.fandom.com/wiki/Prismatic_Trials , https://riskofrain2.fandom.com/wiki/Eclipse , https://www.reddit.com/r/riskofrain/ (Prismatic leaderboard complaint threads)
monetization_context: Pure BUY-TO-PLAY with NO microtransactions and NO ads on the canonical PC/console product -- strongly aligned with Abyssal Lantern's 'no monetization ever' stance in spirit (a one-time purchase, not F2P). Base game (~$24.99, originally $19.99 in 2019 Early Access) plus optional paid DLC EXPANSIONS: Survivors of the Void (2022, 2 survivors/40+ items/4 stages/new mode/alt ending -- well received), Seekers of the Storm (2024, 3 survivors/8+ items/5 stages/skins -- mixed-to-controversial reception over quality/balance/bugs), and Alloyed Collective (2025, 2 survivors/18 items/7 stages/alt ending). Notable co-op courtesy: only ONE player in a lobby needs a DLC for everyone to see its stages/monsters/items (non-owners just can't pick the new survivors or permanently unlock the items). Commercial scale: 1M copies in the first month of EA (2019), 4M+ on Steam by March 2021. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_of_Rain_2 , https://store.steampowered.com/app/632360/Risk_of_Rain_2/ , https://www.pcgamer.com/risk-of-rain-2-sales/ , https://www.gamespot.com/
community_praise: Exceptional moment-to-moment action-combat feel and the euphoric power-fantasy snowball; genuine build creativity from item synergies/proc chains; huge replayability from survivors x items x Eclipse x looping; fair skill-expression (manual aim + dodging rewards mastery); generous co-op DLC sharing; frequent free content and long post-launch support; 'Very Positive'/'Overwhelmingly Positive' Steam standing. Widely cited as the benchmark for the 3D action-roguelite subgenre. Sources: https://store.steampowered.com/app/632360/Risk_of_Rain_2/ , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_of_Rain_2 , https://www.reddit.com/r/riskofrain/
community_complaints: (1) 'Delete or be deleted' / one-shot late-game meta -- once you out-scale, runs become trivial screen-wipes with no tension; if you fall behind you get instantly deleted (the core GAP-C symptom). (2) SOLVED-BUILD & item-pool issues -- a handful of auto-pick items dominate, the Command artifact lets players remove all variety, and a bloated pool dilutes finding your key pieces. (3) Prismatic Trials leaderboard is broken/cheated/unreliable, undermining the recurring hook. (4) NO meaningful failure reward / grindy per-survivor Eclipse -- some players dislike restarting from zero and re-climbing E1-E8 on every character. (5) Seekers of the Storm launch was buggy and balance-controversial. (6) Performance/lag once proc-chain builds spawn thousands of on-hit effects. Sources: https://www.reddit.com/r/riskofrain/ , https://steamcommunity.com/app/632360/discussions/ , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_of_Rain_2
relevance_to_abyssal: GAP-A (finite ceiling): Eclipse (E1-E8) is a proven CLEAR-TO-UNLOCK modifier ladder that gives post-campaign power somewhere to be spent WITHOUT any endless treadmill or numeric prestige -- each rung is a fixed, hand-authored handicap you must WIN once to advance (E1 -50% start HP, E5 -50% healing, E8 max-HP-drain-on-hit). ADOPT: after the Echo Throne clear, add an 'Eclipse-style' handicap ladder (e.g. 8 stacking modifiers) re-running the SAME 3 zones/bosses -- fully deterministic (fixed modifier sets, no RNG scaling), single-player, and it converts 'excess Warden power' into a difficulty target instead of demanding new content. AVOID RoR2's continuous time-coefficient looping model: infinite auto-scaling fits their long sessions but breaks our tight 5-8 min telegraphed-boss design and determinism goals. GAP-B (retention / why-come-back): Prismatic Trials is a concrete NON-MONETIZED daily/recurring hook -- a FIXED shared seed (identical map/items/enemies for all players) that rotates on a timer with a leaderboard, turning a roguelite into a fair daily skill-optimization puzzle. ADOPT: a 'Daily Echo' -- one deterministic seed per day (our seed-based PCG already supports this trivially), same cell layout + skill-drop offers for everyone, scored by clear time / boss no-hit, with a local + optional friends board. Our deterministic 60Hz sim makes replay verification and anti-cheat FAR cleaner than RoR2's. HEED THE WARNING: RoR2's leaderboard is cheated/broken/mod-disabled -- with a deterministic replay we can validate runs server-lessly and avoid that failure. GAP-C (solved-build risk): RoR2 is the strongest CAUTIONARY tale -- exponential/effectively-multiplicative item stacking + proc chains produce runaway 'delete-everything' builds, and the Command artifact (deterministic build assembly) shows that letting players hand-pick the dominant combo kills variety. AVOID for our 20-skill tier system: do NOT let melee-amp/aoe-burst multipliers stack multiplicatively or let one skill's effect trigger another's proc (no chain amplification), or a single T3 loadout will trivialize every run exactly like Shaped-Glass/proc RoR2. ADOPT the defensive levers RoR2 lacks: hyperbolic/diminishing stacking (their Tougher Times model that asymptotes and never trivializes), per-category soft caps, and using our respec + 6-slot limit to force opportunity-cost choices rather than 'assemble the known-broken build every time.'
